extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators, environmental compliance staff, and monitoring personnel at bulk gasoline terminals and gasoline loading facilities
extracted.subtask_short: bulk gasoline terminal monitoring and reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for installation, operation, calibration, testing, recordkeeping, and reporting of monitoring systems, leak detection, annual certification, flare/thermal oxidation monitoring, and limited alternatives at bulk gasoline terminals and gasoline loading facilities under the NSPS subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: TOC CEMS performance and RATA requirements (FID)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CEMS uses a flame ionization detector, the CEMS must be installed, evaluated, and operated according to the requirements of Performance Specification 8A of appendix B to this part. As part of the performance evaluation, conduct a relative accuracy test audit (RATA) following the procedures in Performance Specification 2, section 8.4, of appendix B to this part; the relative accuracy must meet the criteria of Performance Specification 8, section 13.2, of appendix B to this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method 25A in appendix A-7 must be used as the reference method, and the calibration gas must be propane. Owner/operator may exclude methane following specified procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methane exclusion procedure for TOC (chromatographic separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methane must be separated using a chromatographic column and measured by the flame ionization detector, followed by a back-flush of the chromatographic column to directly measure TOC concentration minus methane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When excluding methane, the CEMS must otherwise meet Performance Specification 8A requirements; perform RATA per Performance Specification 2 (section 8.4) and meet relative accuracy criteria in Performance Specification 8 (section 13.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference method selection for TOC minus methane
rubrics_metrics.description: If the concentration of TOC minus methane in the exhaust stream is greater than 50 ppmv, Method 25 must be used as the reference method and calibration gas must be propane; if 50 ppmv or less, Method 25A must be used and calibration gas must be propane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Method 25A is the reference method, procedures in paragraph (c)(6) may be used to subtract methane from the TOC concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: TOC minus methane recording frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: The TOC concentration minus methane must be recorded at least once every 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection methods allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct leak detection monitoring using either Method 21 in appendix A-7 to this part or OGI according to all requirements in appendix K to this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct the leak detection specified in §60.502a(j)(1) for the collection of equipment at a bulk gasoline terminal affected facility using one of the procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 21 leak definition and instrument calibration gases
rubrics_metrics.description: For Method 21, the instrument reading that defines a leak is 10,000 ppmv (as methane). The instrument shall be calibrated before use each day of its use by the procedures specified in Method 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use zero air (<10 ppm hydrocarbon) and methane in air at 10,000 ppm as calibration gases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 21 daily drift assessment and re-monitoring thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of each monitoring day, check instrument using same calibration gas used before use; compute calibration drift as percent difference between initial and post-test response divided by calibration gas value. If negative drift >10%, re-monitor all equipment monitored since last calibration with readings between the leak definition and leak_definition*(100 - percent_negative_drift)/100. If positive drift >10%, owner/operator may re-monitor equipment with readings above leak_definition and below leak_definition*(100 + percent_positive_drift)/100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures in Method 21 section 10.1 except do not adjust meter readout to correspond to calibration gas value. If multiple scales used, record reading for each; calculate arithmetic difference per scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: OGI leak definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For OGI, a leak is defined as any emissions plume imaged by the camera from equipment regulated by this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual cargo tank certification test (Method 27) — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual certification test for gasoline cargo tanks shall consist of Method 27 using a time period (t) for the pressure and vacuum tests of 5 minutes. Initial pressure Pi = 460 mm H2O (18 in. H2O) gauge; initial vacuum Vi = 150 mm H2O (6 in. H2O) gauge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum allowable pressure and vacuum changes (Δp, Δv) are specified in a table by tank capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual cargo tank allowable pressure/vacuum change by capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of allowable gasoline cargo tank test pressure or vacuum change over 5 minutes: 2,500+ gallons: 12.7 mm H2O (0.50 in.); 1,500–2,499: 19.1 mm H2O (0.75 in.); 1,000–1,499: 25.4 mm H2O (1.00 in.); 999 or less: 31.8 mm H2O (1.25 in).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure test of gasoline cargo tank internal vapor valve
rubrics_metrics.description: After Method 27 tests, repressurize tank to 460 mm H2O, close internal vapor valve(s) to isolate vapor return line/manifold, relieve pressure in vapor return line to atmospheric, reseal line, wait 5 minutes, record gauge pressure. Maximum allowable 5-minute pressure increase is 65 mm H2O (2.5 in. H2O).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative to Method 27
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to paragraph (f)(1) (Method 27), you may use the procedure in §63.425(i) of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combustion zone CPMS installation location
rubrics_metrics.description: Install the temperature CPMS in the combustion (flame) zone or in the exhaust gas stream as close as practical to the combustion burners in a position that provides a representative temperature of the combustion zone of the thermal oxidation system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combustion zone CPMS accuracy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The temperature CPMS must be capable of measuring temperature with an accuracy of ±1 percent over the normal range of temperatures measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combustion zone CPMS recording and averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: The temperature CPMS must be capable of recording the temperature at least once every 5 minutes and calculating hourly block averages that include only those 5‑minute periods in which liquid product was loaded into gasoline cargo tanks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combustion zone CPMS inspection and calibration frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: At least quarterly, inspect all components for integrity and electrical connections for continuity, oxidation, and galvanic corrosion (unless CPMS has redundant temperature sensor). Conduct calibration checks at least annually and after any period >24 hours during which the temperature exceeded manufacturer's specified maximum rated temperature or install a new temperature sensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor recovery TOC CEMS installation, QA, and performance evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Install, calibrate, operate, and maintain a CEMS for measuring TOC in atmospheric vent from vapor recovery systems per Performance Specification 8 (or 8A if FID), Procedure 1 QA in appendix F, and procedures under §60.13. For CEMS certified using Performance Spec 8A, conduct RATA as required under Procedure 1 according to §60.503a(d). Conduct annual performance evaluations per §60.503a(d), accuracy determinations quarterly, and calibration drift tests daily per Procedure 1 in appendix F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate sampling probe to obtain representative measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: TOC CEMS span requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The span value of the TOC CEMS must be approximately 2 times the applicable emission limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare CPMS and monitoring substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Install, operate, and maintain CPMS for flares used to comply with emission limitations, including monitors for gasoline and total liquid product loading rates, following requirements in §63.671; substitute 'pilot flame or flare flame' for occurrences of 'pilot flame.' Conduct visible emission observations as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous process mass spectrometer option for net heating value
rubrics_metrics.description: You may determine compositional analysis for net heating value with a continuous process mass spectrometer without use of a gas chromatograph if you meet the specific requirements (paragraphs (c)(2)(i)–(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include meeting §63.671(e)(2), augmenting calibration gas list as needed, calibration cylinders certified to 2% accuracy traceable to NIST, initial calibration to identify overlaps/response factors, and meeting Performance Specification 9 continuous monitoring acceptance requirements (initial multi-point calibration and periodic calibration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unknown gas components for mass spectrometer
rubrics_metrics.description: For unknowns with similar analytical mass fragments to calibration compounds, report unknowns as increase in overlapped calibration compound; for unknowns that do not overlap, use response factor for nearest molecular weight hydrocarbon; may use n-pentane response factor for unknowns heavier than n-pentane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument calibration error (CE) limits for mass spectrometer and NHV
rubrics_metrics.description: The average instrument calibration error (CE) for each calibration compound at any calibration concentration must not differ by more than 10% from the certified cylinder gas value. Alternatively, if using CE of net heating value (NHV) measured vs cylinder tag NHV, CE for NHV at any calibration level must not differ by more than 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CE is calculated per provided equations; meet Performance Specification 9 acceptance and periodic calibration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible emissions observation trigger and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: If visible emissions are observed for more than one continuous minute during normal duties, conduct Method 22 visible emissions observation for 2 hours or until 5 minutes of visible emissions are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure CPMS specification and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Install a pressure CPMS (liquid manometer, magnehelic gauge, or equivalent) capable of measuring up to 500 mm of water gauge pressure with ±2.5 mm of water precision on the terminal's vapor collection system at a pressure tap located as close as possible to the connection with the gasoline cargo tank. Install multiple pressure CPMS at each loading rack if necessary to obtain representative loading pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure CPMS calibration, inspection, and output review
rubrics_metrics.description: Check calibration of the pressure CPMS at least annually and after any period >24 hours during which pressure exceeded manufacturer's maximum rated pressure (or install a new sensor). At least quarterly, visually inspect components for integrity, oxidation and galvanic corrosion (unless redundant sensor). Review CPMS output each operating day to ensure expected fluctuations; repair/unplug plugged pressure taps within 24 hours or prior to next gasoline cargo tank loading, whichever is longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited alternative monitoring when TOC CEMS offline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the TOC CEMS is off-line for >15 minutes for maintenance, you may use monitoring of product loading quantities and regeneration cycle parameters as an alternative to the CEMS monitoring for no more than 240 hours in a calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine product loading operating limit as the smallest of the past 10 adsorption cycles prior to outage. Determine average vacuum pressure, purge gas quantities, and duration from past 10 desorption cycles and operate desorption cycles at or above these averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period general
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records specified for each affected facility for a minimum of five years unless otherwise specified; these recordkeeping requirements supersede §60.7(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required CMS record elements (limits, averages, deviations, outages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of: (i) applicable operating or emission limit for CMS (include date ranges for combustion zone temperature limits); (ii) each 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature, each 5-minute average pressure reading, and each 3-hour rolling average TOC concentration (as propane); (iii) for each deviation of 3-hour rolling average temperature limit, max loading pressure, or 3-hour rolling average TOC concentration, record start date/time, duration, cause, and corrective action; (iv) for each CMS outage or out-of-control period, record start date/time, duration, cause, and corrective action (for TOC CEMS outages using limited alternative include indication of use of alternative).

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS inspection/calibration records and TOC CEMS specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: For each inspection or calibration of CMS include a unique identifier, make, and model number of the CMS, and date of calibration check. For TOC CEMS, include type (e.g., FID, NDIR) and indicate whether methane is excluded from the TOC concentration reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records required when using limited alternative for TOC CEMS outage
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of the quantity of liquid product loaded in gasoline cargo tanks for the past 10 adsorption cycles prior to outage; vacuum pressure, purge gas quantities, and duration for past 10 desorption cycles prior to outage; quantity loaded for each adsorption cycle while using alternative; vacuum/purge/duration for each desorption cycle while using alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare and thermal oxidation system recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records for flares and thermal oxidation systems including: (i) output of pilot-flame presence monitor for minimum 2 years and retain records of 15-minute blocks with at least one minute no pilot flame present when gasoline vapors routed to flare for 5 years; (ii) visible emissions observations (Method 22) records for min 3 years; (iii) each 15-minute block period when operating values outside applicable operating limits while loading for at least 15 minutes; (iv) 15-minute block average cumulative flows and assist gas monitoring records retention times specified (2 or 5 years depending on data); (v) flare vent gas or thermal oxidation vent gas compositions retention (2 years individual component concentrations; NHV_vg analyzer 15-minute averages for 5 years); (vi) 15-minute block average operating parameters calculated per §63.670(k)–(n); (vii) all periods when monitoring procedures not performed (start date/time/duration); (viii) indication whether 'vapors displaced...' excludes certain periods and records of such periods; (ix) retain one-time flare tip velocity compliance assessment records while using that compliance method; (x) CMS parameter deviation/outage/inspection calibration records as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple monitoring locations used, retain 15-minute block average flows for each location for minimum 2 years, and cumulative flows used in subsequent calculations for minimum 5 years. If using supplemental gas flow monitoring alternative, retain required and actual supplemental gas flow rates for minimum 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gasoline cargo tank vapor tightness documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep vapor tightness documentation for each gasoline cargo tank loading on file at the terminal (hardcopy or electronic) including: test title, cargo tank owner's name/address, cargo tank ID number, test location/date, tester name/signature, witnessing inspector (if any), vapor tightness repair description and timing, and test results (capacity, test pressure, pressure/vacuum change, test time, number of leaks, leak definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records when vapor tightness documentation missing
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of each instance where liquid product loaded into a gasoline cargo tank without required vapor tightness documentation must include cargo tank owner/address, tank ID, date/time of loading without documentation, and date proper documentation was received or statement that documentation was never received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records for loading deviations (no submerged filling, incompatible or improperly connected equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of each instance when liquid product loaded into tanks not using submerged filling, not equipped with compatible vapor collection equipment, or not properly connected must include date/time, type of deviation (e.g., not submerged filling, incompatible equipment, not properly connected), and cargo tank ID number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory of equipment in gasoline service and leak inspection records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a record (list, summary, or diagrams) of all equipment in gasoline service at the collection of equipment and loading rack facilities, and a record of each leak inspection and each leak identified with specific information per paragraphs (a)(6)(i)–(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each leak inspection indicate whether conducted under §§60.502a(j) or 60.503a(a)(2) and leak determination method used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 21-specific leak inspection record elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For leak inspections conducted with Method 21, keep date of inspection, inspector name, monitoring instrument identification, identification of all equipment surveyed and instrument reading for each, date/time of instrument calibration and initials of operator, calibration gas cylinder identification/certification date/certified concentration, instrument scale used, and results of daily calibration drift assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: OGI-specific leak inspection records
rubrics_metrics.description: For leak inspections conducted with OGI, keep the records specified in section 12 of appendix K to this part (e.g., video footage for repair confirmation when OGI used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak repair and delayed repair records
rubrics_metrics.description: For each leak detected, record equipment type/ID, date found, name of person who found leak, nature of leak (vapor or liquid), method of detection, dates of each repair attempt and methods used, date of successful repair and method of monitoring to confirm repair (Method 21 maximum instrument reading or OGI video footage if used). For repairs delayed beyond 15 calendar days after discovery, record 'Repair delayed', reason for delay, expected date of successful repair and signature of decision maker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each leak determined not repairable, record maximum Method 21 reading at determination, OGI video showing emissions still visible, or signed record that leak still detectable via audio/visual/olfactory methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test/evaluation records and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain records of each performance test or performance evaluation and each notification/report submitted to the Administrator; for each performance test include indication whether liquid product loading is assumed to be loaded into gasoline cargo tanks or whether periods when liquid product is loaded but no gasoline cargo tanks are being loaded are excluded in setting the combustion zone temperature operating limit per §60.503a(c)(8)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑minute loading period records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of all 5‑minute time periods during which liquid product is loaded into gasoline cargo tanks or assumed to be loaded, and records of all 5‑minute time periods when there was no liquid product loaded into gasoline cargo tanks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic record submission allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Records required by this subpart that are submitted electronically via EPA's CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format; this does not affect requirement to make records/data/reports available upon request during on-site compliance evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning July 8, 2024 (or once report template on CEDRI available for one year), submit reports via CEDRI template; dates templates become available will be listed on CEDRI website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test and CEMS performance evaluation reporting deadline and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after completing each performance test and each CEMS performance evaluation required by this subpart, submit results following specified procedures. Include combustion zone temperature operating parameter limit set based on performance test in performance test report. Data collected using ERT‑supported test methods or CEMS RATA pollutants must be submitted in ERT file format or XML schema; unsupported test methods must be included as attachment in ERT or alternate electronic file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As required by §60.8(f)(2)(iv) include the value for the combustion zone temperature operating parameter limit in the performance test report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual report contents and submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit semiannual reports to Administrator with required information (facility general information; CMS deviation and outage details; counts of specific deviations while using limited alternative; and other elements) by dates specified; reports supersede excess emissions and monitoring systems performance/summary reports under §60.7; beginning July 8, 2024 (or one year after CEDRI template availability) submit subsequent reports using CEDRI template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General facility information required includes facility name, physical address, decimals latitude/longitude (≥5 decimal places), contact person info, reporting period dates, and responsible official statement/certification (electronic signature via CEDRI replaces paper signature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual CMS reporting detail elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each thermal oxidation system, pressure CPMS, and vapor recovery system CMS report: for instances of measurements beyond limits provide date/start time, duration, measurements during deviation (3‑hour avg temp, avg pressure, or 3‑hour avg TOC), CMS unique identifier, make/model, date of last calibration, cause and corrective action; for CMS outages/out-of-control events provide date/start time, duration, CMS unique identifier, make/model, date of last calibration, cause and corrective action; for TOC CEMS outages where limited alternative used, report either indication of no deviations while using alternative or counts of four specific types of deviations during alternative use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts requested: (1) adsorption cycles exceeding operating limit; (2) desorption cycles below average vacuum pressure; (3) desorption cycles with purge gas below average quantity; (4) desorption cycles with duration less than average duration. Enter 0 if none.
